_comment: The MACHINERY register: the completeness AND conformance authority for machine PERFORMANCE. The equipment register says a machine exists and MachineValidator says its shell is the right shape; NEITHER says it BEHAVES as the real machine did. This register closes that gap. Every machine that moves, heats, flows or spins carries its performance quantities here, each with a source and a status, and each tied to the exact constant in PlantPhysics.java that the code uses. The self-test (MachineryRegisterSelfTest) then asserts the code's value EQUALS the value recorded here, so a performance number cannot silently drift: if someone edits MCP_FLOW_RATED_M3S, the test fails until the register is updated to a new SOURCED value. That is the machine-checkable answer to 'what if the feedwater pump does not have the same flow rate as reality?'. Status is one of: verified (cites a primary source with url + quote), to_verify (a reference value not yet confirmed against a primary source), placeholder (no source; a fallback only). The spine sources are the operating regulation (Reglament 1E-S-II, 1983), NUREG-1250, INSAG-7, and the plant-systems reference docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md (keyed WP).

_statusLegend.verified: cites a primary source, with sourceUrl + quote
_statusLegend.to_verify: a reference value not yet confirmed against a primary source
_statusLegend.placeholder: a value with no source at all; allowed only as a fallback

items.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §2 (keyed WP §86): 'Pump capacity 5,500-12,000 m3/h; nominal 8,000 m3/h'. NUREG-1250 §2.2.2 corroborates the pump set.
items.note: The single number that sets the whole coolant mass flow (6 running x 8,000 m3/h = 48,000 m3/h). If this is wrong, the void, the power and the accident are all wrong.

items.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §2 (keyed WP §86): 'Throttled flow (<500 MWt) 6,000-7,000 m3/h per pump'; 6,500 is the midpoint of that sourced band.
items.note: INSAG-7 §2.9 describes the throttling during low-power phases of startup/shutdown. The band is sourced; the midpoint is chosen.

items.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §2 (keyed WP §86): 'Pump motor 6 kV electric'. The 6 MW figure is a reference; the voltage is sourced.
items.note: Sets the pump coast-down energy budget after a trip.

items.source: INSAG-7 §2.9 (the rundown that, after Chernobyl, was arranged to drive the ECCS pumps). The 8 s constant is a reference, not a cited measurement.
items.note: The flywheel rundown. After Chernobyl the rundown energy was specifically arranged to run the ECCS; the exact tau is not pinned to a primary source.

items.source: INSAG-7 §2.6 and NUREG-1250: the RBMK-1000 is 3,200 MWt / 1,000 MWe. The plant-systems reference carries it as the rated power.
items.note: The denominator of every power fraction.

items.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §4 (keyed WP §136): 'Turbogenerators per unit: 2, each 500 MWe; turbine model K-500-65/3000'.
items.note: Two per unit give the 1,000 MWe net.

items.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §4 (keyed WP §136): 'Speed 3,000 rpm'. Standard 50 Hz synchronous speed.
items.note: The name K-500-65/3000 encodes the 3,000 rpm.

items.source: Derived from the plant figures: 1,000 MWe / 3,200 MWt = 0.3125; 0.33 is the rounded reference value.
items.note: Consistency check: 2 x 500 MWe / 3,200 MWt = 0.3125, so 0.33 is slightly optimistic. Flagged.

items.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §3 (keyed WP §83): 'Diameter 2.8 m; Length 31 m; Wall 100 mm'.
items.note: Sets the drum volume, hence the level dynamics and the level trips.
With the diameter, sets the drum mass and the level response.

items.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §3 (keyed WP §84): 'Steam quality at outlet ~15%'. Corroborated by the channel energy balance in ChannelCooling (10,000 kg/s, 320 kJ/kg -> ~15.6% outlet quality).
items.quote: The mass steam content at the exit from the ... separators ... 14-15%
items.note: The same figure drives the derived void in the core; a single source feeds both.

items.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §5 (deaerators as reservoir, WP §91). The 1,500 kg/s figure is a reference; it must match the steam production at full power.
items.note: Consistency check: steam flow per turbine 82,880 t/h / 2 = ~11,511 kg/s per... (needs checking against the separator balance). Flagged to_verify.

items.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §4 (keyed WP §136): 'Steam flow per turbine 82,880 t/h'. Reused here as the cooling-water flow order.
items.note: The 82,880 t/h is the TURBINE STEAM flow; using it as the condenser cooling-water flow is a reference assumption. Flagged.

items.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §5. A reference figure for the condenser terminal difference.
INSAG-7 §2.9 and docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §2 (keyed WP §83): 'Two independent cooling circuits, each serving one half of the reactor'.
items.note: Two halves; each with its own pumps, headers and separators.

items.source: docs/RBMK-PLANT-SYSTEMS.md §2 (keyed WP §83): 'Pumps per circuit 4 (3 running, 1 standby); total 8 (6 running)'.
items.quote: eight main circulating pumps ... six of which were operating
items.note: The loss of two MCPs on one side was a reactor trip (INSAG-7 §2.9).
